events.title: Cathy Ames is introduced as a born monster
events.summary: The narrator presents young Cathy as someone born without ordinary conscience, who manipulates everyone around her. She ends her childhood by burning down her parents' house with them inside and vanishing.
events.citation: I believe there are monsters born in the world to human parents
events.rationale: This is the nature Cal later fears he has inherited. His dread of the 'bad blood' in him, and his wish to use it against Aron, starts here.
events.for_cal: Cal will one day learn that his mother is this woman, and fear that her coldness lives in him.

events.title: Cathy marries Adam and goes to Charles on the wedding night
events.summary: Beaten and taken in at the Trask farm, Cathy marries the smitten Adam. On their wedding night she drugs him and goes to his brother Charles's bed.
events.rationale: The marriage produces the twins and leaves even their fatherhood uncertain. It ties Cal to a mother who never loved his father.
events.for_cal: Cal is born from a marriage built on his mother's deceit, a secret kept from him.

events.title: The twins are born and Cathy rejects them
events.summary: Samuel Hamilton delivers Cathy's twin boys. Cathy bites his hand during the birth and shows no interest in the babies.
events.rationale: Cal begins life unwanted by his mother. That rejection becomes the hidden wound behind his later behavior.
events.for_cal: From birth Cal is unwanted by his mother, though he will not know it for years.

events.title: Cathy shoots Adam and abandons the twins
events.summary: About a week after the birth, Cathy tells Adam she is leaving. When he tries to stop her, she shoots him in the shoulder and walks out, leaving the infants behind.
events.rationale: The mother's desertion creates the empty space and the lie that shape Cal's childhood. It also sets up the truth he later uses as a weapon.
events.for_cal: Cal loses his mother as a baby and grows up without knowing why.

events.title: Adam hides the truth about the shooting
events.summary: When Deputy Horace Quinn questions him, the wounded Adam insists the shooting was an accident. He tries to shield Cathy and keep her flight hidden.
events.rationale: Adam's habit of hiding Cathy's truth starts here. It grows into the family lie that Cal later breaks open.
events.for_cal: The silence that will surround Cal's mother throughout his childhood begins here.

events.title: Cathy becomes 'Kate' at Faye's brothel in Salinas
events.summary: Cathy goes to Salinas, takes the name Kate, and joins Faye's brothel. She soon makes herself indispensable to its owner.
events.rationale: It puts Cal's mother, under another name, in the very town where the boys will later live. That makes Cal's discovery and the later visit with Aron possible.
events.for_cal: Cal's mother is living a few miles away under a new name, a secret waiting for him.

events.title: Adam sinks into apathy while Lee raises the twins
events.summary: For more than a year Adam barely looks at his sons and has not even named them. Lee, the Chinese servant, cares for the boys.
events.rationale: Cal's earliest life is marked by a father who hardly sees him. Lee becomes his true guide, a bond that matters right up to the focal night.
events.for_cal: Cal's first years are spent with an absent-minded father and a loving servant, Lee, in his place.

events.title: Samuel strikes Adam to wake him
events.summary: Samuel, furious at Adam's neglect of the boys, knocks him down. The blow shocks Adam back toward responsibility.
events.rationale: It forces Adam to take up fatherhood, however imperfectly. Cal will spend his youth trying to win that father's love.
events.for_cal: Cal's father is forced to start paying attention to him, but only partly.

events.title: The twins are named after a talk about Cain and Abel
events.summary: Samuel, Adam and Lee read and debate the story of Cain and Abel while choosing names. The boys become Caleb and Aron.
events.rationale: The naming frames Cal as the Cain figure, the son whose gift is rejected and who strikes at his brother. The focal night replays that pattern.
events.for_cal: Cal is given a name tied to the Cain-and-Abel story he will half-live out with Aron.

events.title: Lee explains that rejection breeds rage and guilt
events.summary: Lee argues that the Cain story is everyone's story. A child's deepest terror is not being loved, and rejection leads to anger, crime and guilt.
events.citation: The greatest terror a child can have is that he is not loved
events.rationale: Lee spells out the very mechanism that drives Cal after Adam refuses his gift. It explains why that refusal makes Cal lash out at Aron.
events.for_cal: Lee forms an idea of the rejected son that will guide how he raises and counsels Cal.

events.title: Lee's elders arrive at 'timshel', thou mayest
events.summary: Lee reports that his elderly Chinese relatives studied Hebrew to understand the Cain verse. They concluded the word timshel means 'thou mayest', so humans can choose to overcome sin.
events.rationale: Lee carries this belief in free choice into his later talks with Cal. Cal's sense that he alone is to blame for what he does comes from it.
events.for_cal: Lee forms the belief in personal choice that he will later pass on to Cal.

events.title: Samuel tells Adam that Cathy runs a Salinas brothel
events.summary: On his farewell visit, Samuel tells Adam that Cathy is alive in Salinas, calling herself Kate and running a brothel. He hopes the truth will free Adam.
events.rationale: The adults now know where the boys' mother is, yet keep it from them. That deepens the secret Cal will uncover alone.
events.for_cal: The adults around Cal now know his mother's whereabouts and will keep it from him.

events.title: Adam confronts Kate and is freed from her
events.summary: Adam visits Kate at her brothel. She taunts him and boasts of her hold over powerful men, but he sees her clearly and walks out released from her spell.
events.rationale: Freed, Adam can live again, yet he still hides Kate from his sons. Cal will have to face this mother on his own.
events.for_cal: Cal's father comes back to life but keeps the truth about Cal's mother locked away.

events.title: Abra visits and warms to Aron's gift
events.summary: A rainstorm strands young Abra and her parents at the Trask place. Abra is drawn to gentle Aron, who gives her a rabbit, and Cal feels pushed aside.
events.rationale: This first episode of others preferring Aron over Cal feeds the jealousy and sense of being less loved that explode on the focal night.
events.for_cal: Cal feels that people naturally love Aron more than him, and resents it.

events.title: Abra tells Aron his mother is not dead
events.summary: Abra repeats what she overheard from her parents: the twins' mother did not die but ran away. This challenges the story the boys were told.
events.rationale: It plants the first doubt about their mother in the boys' world. It also shows that Aron's need for a pure, idealized mother is fragile.
events.for_cal: Cal begins to sense that the story of his dead mother may be a lie.

events.title: Cal prays not to be mean
events.summary: Alone at night, Cal asks God to make him like Aron and not mean. He promises anything if people will love him.
events.rationale: It shows the core of Cal: a hunger to be loved, matched with shame at his own cruelty. Both are at work when he hurts Aron years later.
events.for_cal: Cal fears he is mean by nature and desperately wants to be loved like Aron.

events.title: Adam's iced-lettuce venture fails
events.summary: Adam ships lettuce east in iced railroad cars, but the train is delayed and the crop rots. He loses much of his fortune and becomes a laughingstock in Salinas.
events.rationale: Cal later aims to earn back this lost money as a gift for his father. That gift's rejection triggers the focal event.
events.for_cal: Cal sees his father humiliated and poorer, and later wants to make it up to him.

events.title: Aron turns devout and plans the ministry
events.summary: Under the influence of the Episcopal minister Mr. Rolf, Aron becomes intensely religious. He talks of becoming a minister and swears off worldly impurity.
events.rationale: Cal knows Aron's purity cannot bear the truth about their mother. That is exactly why showing him Kate is such a devastating blow.
events.for_cal: Cal watches his brother build a pure, protected world that the truth about their mother could shatter.

events.title: Cal discovers that the madam Kate is his mother
events.summary: Restless and sleepless, Cal roams Salinas at night. Through the town's talk he learns that Kate, owner of the notorious brothel, is his mother.
events.rationale: This is the secret Cal will eventually turn against Aron. It also feeds his fear that he carries her badness.
events.for_cal: Cal learns his mother is a brothel keeper and fears her evil is in him.

events.title: Lee tells Cal the truth and that his choices are his own
events.summary: When Cal presses him, Lee confirms who Kate is and tells him the story of his parents. Lee insists Cal has his father in him as well, and that whatever he does will be his own doing, not his mother's.
events.rationale: Lee takes away Cal's excuse of bad blood and makes him responsible for his acts. On the focal night Cal acts knowing the choice is his.
events.for_cal: Cal learns he cannot blame his mother's blood for what he does; he is free and responsible.

events.title: Cal follows Kate and confronts her
events.summary: Cal trails Kate on her walks until she brings him into her room. She tries to draw him in as someone like herself and asks about Aron. Cal sees her fear and leaves no longer afraid of her.
events.rationale: Cal now knows Kate in person and knows the way to her house. He is the only son who has faced her, which lets him lead Aron there later.
events.for_cal: Cal meets his mother, refuses to be like her, and keeps the secret from Aron.

events.title: Adam serves on the wartime draft board
events.summary: When America enters the First World War, Adam sits on the local draft board. He is troubled by the young men he sends off to fight.
events.rationale: Adam's guilt over sending boys to die makes him reject money earned from wartime prices. That rejection pushes Cal to the focal act.
events.for_cal: Cal's father grows morally burdened by the war in a way that will turn against Cal's gift.

events.title: Cal partners with Will Hamilton to grow beans
events.summary: Cal goes to the businessman Will Hamilton with a plan to grow and sell beans while wartime demand is high. He hopes to rebuild the money his father lost.
events.rationale: The venture produces the gift Cal hopes will finally earn Adam's love. Its rejection sets off his revenge on Aron.
events.for_cal: Cal hopes to win his father's love by earning back what he lost.

events.title: Lee lends Cal the money to start
events.summary: Cal needs five thousand dollars for his share of the bean deal. Lee gives it to him from his own savings.
events.rationale: Lee's trust makes the gift possible and shows Cal that someone believes in him. That makes the coming rejection by Adam sting harder.
events.for_cal: Cal is trusted with Lee's savings and feels his plan to please his father can work.

events.title: Adam glows with pride over Aron's college plans
events.summary: Aron pushes to finish high school early and enter Stanford. Adam is openly proud of him.
events.rationale: Adam's open delight in Aron sharpens Cal's sense of being the less loved son. Adam measures Cal against Aron at the Thanksgiving dinner.
events.for_cal: Cal sees his father lavish pride on Aron and feels himself overlooked.

events.title: Aron goes away to Stanford
events.summary: Aron leaves home early for Stanford, carrying his father's hopes. Cal stays behind in Salinas.
events.rationale: Aron's absence makes his return at Thanksgiving a special occasion. Cal plans his gift for that same day, so the brothers are measured side by side.
events.for_cal: With Aron gone and praised from afar, Cal plans a gift to win a share of his father's pride.

events.title: Cal makes a fortune and plans a Thanksgiving gift
events.summary: The bean deal earns Cal fifteen thousand dollars. He gets the money in new bills and plans to give it to Adam at Thanksgiving dinner, when Aron is home.
events.rationale: All of Cal's hope of being loved is poured into this gift. Its rejection is the immediate trigger of the focal event.
events.for_cal: Cal believes this gift will finally make his father love him.

events.title: Adam rejects Cal's money and praises Aron instead
events.summary: At Thanksgiving, Cal gives Adam the money. Adam refuses it as profit made from the war while he sends boys to die. He says the gift he wants is a good life like Aron's.
events.citation: I would have been so happy if you could have given me
events.rationale: This is Cal's Cain moment: his offering is refused and his brother is held up as the better son. His hurt and rage go straight into revealing Kate to Aron.
events.for_cal: Cal feels utterly rejected by his father and blinded by jealousy of Aron.

events.title: Lee tries to steady Cal after the rejection
events.summary: Lee goes to the stricken Cal and urges him not to let his hurt and anger take control of him.
events.rationale: Even with Lee's warning that the choice is his, Cal chooses revenge. That makes the focal act his own deliberate decision.
events.for_cal: Cal is reminded he can master his rage, but his pain is stronger than the warning.

events.title: Cal takes Aron to Kate's house and shows him their mother
events.summary: That night, still raw from his father's rejection, Cal leads Aron to Kate's brothel. There he confronts his brother with the truth that its madam is their mother, Cathy.
events.rationale: This is the focal event: jealousy, inherited fear, rejected love and the hidden truth come together in Cal's act against his brother.
events.for_cal: Cal strikes out at the favored brother by destroying Aron's innocence, and soon will be crushed by guilt.
